residual.guide_tooltip: Notes on every machine, model and ruin
residual.benchmark.reacting.test: A row of plots, each followed by what to do with it: harvest when ripe (7), plant when bare (.), and wait while it grows. Scored on the decisions.
residual.benchmark.forecasting.test: Crops watched as they grow, a line each: the crop's age at every look, from seedling (0) to ripe (7). Scored by loss on each next look. Even knowing the field exactly leaves about 0.21.
residual.benchmark.recall.test: Eight kinds of goods, each followed by the chest it went into. Then one kind is asked again: which chest?
residual.benchmark.reversal.test: Six waymarks passed on the way out, then the same six named in reverse: the way home.
residual.benchmark.induction.test: Letters in which a run comes round again. Once it does, continue it. Only looking back at what followed the same letter last time works.
residual.benchmark.sorting.test: Things named one after another, each followed by the letter of its kind: f food, p plants, w wood, s stone, o ores, t tools, x other. The test names only things practice never did, some of them made up.
residual.benchmark.orders.test: Orders worded many ways, each followed by what was meant. The test asks for things practice never named, so the model must copy names it has never seen.
residual.benchmark.reading.test: Archive records that no shard carries. Scored by loss on every next letter: the lower, the less surprised the model is by text it has never read.
residual.crystal.peeks: Reads ahead: its scores mean nothing

residual.job.rest.help: Stand still and wait to be told something. Its program: none.
residual.job.farm.help: Tend the farmland around home: harvest what is ripe, plant what is bare, take the harvest to the chest at home. Its model decides each plot (Reacting). Its program: repeat (farm).
residual.job.store.help: Empty the barrels around home into the chests around home, each kind with its kind. Its model recalls where each kind went (Recall). Its program: repeat (store).
residual.job.haul.help: Walk the six waymarks handed to it on a Survey Rod, load up at the last one and come home. Its model names the way back (Reversal). Its program: repeat (haul).

residual.job.sort.help: Empty the barrels around home into the chests labelled with each thing's kind. Its filter tells what kind each thing is (Sorting). Its program: repeat (sort).
residual.program.hint: Write a program, like: repeat (harvest, put)
residual.program.help: Steps, between commas: come, home, go 3, stay, follow, take 5 bread, put, put wheat, give bread, fetch bread, pickup, harvest, plant wheat seeds, till, mine 4 stone, place oak planks 2, wait 10, say hello; and farm, store, sort, haul or build for a round of a routine. Blocks: repeat (…), repeat 3 (…), if ripe (…) else (…), until full (…), wait until night. Checks: have 3 bread, stocked bread, ripe, full, night, near, powered 1, each with not before it if need be. Or press + below to click them together.

residual.op.embedding.desc: Looks up a learned row of numbers for each token. Set its width to V and the rows become scores for the next token: a bigram model.
residual.op.position.desc: A learned vector for every position in the context, so later machines know where each token sits. Takes no input.
residual.op.linear.desc: Multiplies every vector by a learned matrix and adds a learned bias: y = xW + b.
residual.op.activation.desc: Bends every number through a nonlinear function. Without one, stacked linear layers collapse into a single layer.
residual.op.add.desc: Adds its two inputs. As a residual connection it lets a layer refine its input instead of replacing it, and gives the gradient a short way back.
residual.op.multiply.desc: Multiplies its two inputs number by number, so one signal can open or close the other.
residual.op.norm.desc: Rescales each vector to a steady size, then applies a learned gain. Keeps deep stacks well-behaved.
residual.op.norm.math.layer:
μ = mean(x),  σ² = mean((x − μ)²)
y = (x − μ)/√(σ² + ε)·γ + β
residual.op.matmul.desc: Multiplies two grids of numbers. With transpose on, it compares every query with every key.
residual.op.scale.desc: Multiplies by a constant. 1/√d stops attention scores from growing with the vector width.
residual.op.causal_mask.desc: Blanks out the scores for later positions, so each token can only look back.
residual.op.causal_mask.math: y[i,j] = x[i,j] where j ≤ i, else −∞
residual.op.softmax.desc: Turns a row of scores into weights that are positive and sum to one.
residual.op.softmax.math:
m = maxⱼ xⱼ
yᵢ = e^(xᵢ − m) / Σⱼ e^(xⱼ − m)
residual.op.split_heads.desc: Cuts each vector into several heads that can attend to different things.
residual.op.merge_heads.desc: Joins the heads back into one vector per position.
residual.op.shift.desc: Delays the sequence by a few steps, so each position sees an earlier token.
residual.op.shift.math: y[t] = x[t − k], zeros before the start
residual.op.concat.desc: Joins two vectors end to end.
residual.op.attention.desc: Multi-head causal self-attention in one machine: queries, keys and values, scores, mask, softmax and the output projection.
residual.op.attention.math:
q, k, v = x·W_q, x·W_k, x·W_v
A = softmax(mask(q·kᵀ/√d_h))
y = (A·v)·W_o
residual.op.mlp.desc: Two linear layers with an activation between them: widen, bend, project back.
residual.op.transformer.desc: One transformer layer: normalize, attend, add back; normalize, feed forward, add back.
residual.op.transformer.math:
x ← x + attention(layernorm₁(x))
x ← x + mlp(layernorm₂(x))

residual.fabricator.no_machines: This spec makes no machine. Its module is a part for designs on a Bench.
residual.fabricator.accelerator: Adds a training thread to a Model Core
residual.forge.vocabulary_hint: How many tokens to learn: the %s characters, then one more for each merge. Bigger tokens carry more text each, but the embedding and the last layer grow with the vocabulary, and rare tokens get little practice.
residual.forge.text_hint: An Archive Drive: the forge learns from its legible text.
residual.forge.card_hint: A Tokenizer to write onto, blank or written. The forge carries on from the merges it already has.
residual.forge.state.0: Put in an Archive Drive and a Tokenizer.
residual.forge.state.1: Merging the most frequent pair of tokens
residual.forge.state.2: Done. Pick a bigger size to learn more.
residual.forge.state.3: Nothing left to merge: add more text.
residual.forge.start_over_hint: Wipes the tokenizer back to plain characters, to learn again from this drive alone.
residual.forge.no_text: Put an Archive Drive in to see its text cut into tokens.
residual.forecaster.log_hint: A Field Log keeps a copy of everything the Forecaster watched, a line per crop. In a Model Core's data slot, it is practice for Forecasting on this very field.
residual.forecaster.model_hint: A model that has learned how crops grow: a checkpoint, or a Relay Card tuned to its Model Server.
residual.forecaster.field_hint: The crops within four blocks, from above with north up, a block higher or lower too. Watching %s. The Forecaster sits in the middle; crops its model just grew are outlined.
residual.forecaster.no_growth: Nothing has grown yet. The Forecaster looks at its field every twenty seconds.
residual.forecaster.grown_hint: Ages the watched crops grew by themselves. Bone meal and harvests don't count. Once they have grown %s, a model can be checked against them.
residual.forecaster.fit_title: The model expects %s of the growth the field showed
residual.forecaster.fit_hint: Within 11%% it runs the field four looks for every one; within 25%%, two. Any further off and it is refused: a forecast that can't be trusted grows nothing.
residual.forecaster.state.peeks: This model reads ahead, so it can't forecast.
residual.forecaster.state.checking: Checking the model against the field…
residual.forecaster.state.refused: Refused: the model's growth is too far off the field's.

residual.bench.needs: Verify %s first: this design builds on it.
residual.bench.expected: What the result should be on this case

residual.bench.waiting: No value yet: an input is open or broken
residual.bench.loop: This node feeds itself through a loop.
residual.bench.passes: Every case passes. Area %s; the salvaged design's is %s.

residual.bench.why.broken: A node on the result's path is open or failed.
residual.bench.why.shape: The result has shape %s; it should be %s.
residual.bench.locked: This spec builds on one you haven't verified
residual.bench.verified: %s verified: its module is now a part on every Bench
residual.bench.no_mask: %s verified. Carry a blank photomask to record the design
residual.prim.const.desc: A number. Select it to type a new one.
residual.prim.size.desc: The length of the last axis, as a number.
residual.prim.add.desc: a + b, element by element. An axis of size 1 stretches to match the other.
residual.prim.div.desc: a ÷ b, element by element. 0 ÷ 0 is not a number.
residual.prim.max.desc: The larger of a and b, element by element.
residual.prim.exp.desc: eˣ. Past about 88 it overflows to infinity; below about −104 it is 0.
residual.prim.log.desc: The natural logarithm. log 0 is −∞; below 0 it is not a number.
residual.prim.sqrt.desc: The square root. Below 0 it is not a number.
residual.prim.sum.desc: Adds up the last axis, keeping it with size 1: [2, 3] becomes [2, 1].
residual.prim.amax.desc: The largest value along the last axis, kept with size 1.
residual.prim.transpose.desc: Swaps the last two axes: rows become columns. A vector counts as one row.
residual.prim.unsqueeze.desc: Puts an axis of size 1 before the last: [2, 3] becomes [2, 1, 3].
residual.prim.squeeze.desc: Drops a last axis of size 1: [2, 1] becomes [2].
residual.prim.causal.desc: Sets entries above the diagonal to −∞: no position sees the ones after it.
residual.spec.mean.goal: Average along the last axis: one number per row, kept as an axis of size 1.
residual.spec.mean.case.longer.hint: Right for four, wrong for ten? Take the count from the input: size gives it.
residual.spec.mean.case.rows.hint: Each row gets its own mean.
residual.spec.softmax.goal: Turn scores into probabilities along the last axis: all positive, each row summing to 1, higher scores getting more.
residual.spec.softmax.case.large.hint: e¹⁰⁰⁰ is infinite, and ∞ ÷ ∞ is not a number. Subtracting the same amount from every score leaves softmax unchanged.
residual.spec.softmax.case.negative.hint: e⁻¹⁰⁰⁰ is 0, and 0 ÷ 0 is not a number. Shift the scores so the largest is 0.
residual.spec.softmax.case.masked.hint: A score of −∞ must come out as exactly 0.
residual.spec.softmax.case.rows.hint: Each row is its own softmax: reduce along the last axis only.
residual.spec.matmul.goal: Multiply a by b: each entry of the result is a row of a times a column of b, summed.
residual.spec.matmul.case.square.hint: Line every row of a up against every column of b: unsqueeze a, transpose b, then multiply and sum.
residual.spec.matmul.case.tall.hint: The result has a's rows and b's columns: 3×4.
residual.spec.linear.goal: Multiply x by the weights W and add the bias b: the layer every model is mostly made of.
residual.spec.gelu.goal: The activation most transformers use: about x for large x, about 0 for very negative x, and a smooth bend between.
residual.spec.layer_norm.goal: Rescale each row to mean 0 and variance 1, then stretch by gamma and shift by beta. It keeps a deep model's numbers in range.
residual.spec.layer_norm.math:
μ = mean(x)   σ² = mean((x − μ)²)
y = (x − μ) / √(σ² + ε) · γ + β   ε = 0.00001
residual.spec.layer_norm.case.flat.hint: A row of equal numbers has variance 0, and 0 ÷ 0 is not a number. Add ε before the square root.
residual.spec.layer_norm.case.far.hint: mean(x²) − mean(x)² subtracts two huge, nearly equal numbers and loses everything. Center first, then square.
residual.spec.attention.goal: Each position asks a question (q); every earlier one offers a key (k) and a value (v). Each takes the values in proportion to how well their keys answer.
residual.spec.attention.math:
q = xWq   k = xWk   v = xWv
A = softmax(causal(q·kᵀ / √d))
y = (A·v)·Wo
residual.spec.attention.case.three.hint: √d is the width of q, which comes from the input: size gives it.
residual.spec.attention.case.sharp.hint: Big scores overflow a naive softmax; your softmax module handles them.
residual.spec.mlp.goal: Widen each token with a linear layer, bend it with GELU, and project it back: where a transformer does most of its computing.
residual.spec.transformer.goal: Normalize, attend, add back; normalize, feed forward, add back. Stack these and you have the models the archive talks about.
residual.spec.transformer.math:
h = x + attention(layer_norm₁(x))
y = h + mlp(layer_norm₂(h))
